scope: Independent original-resolution pixel/source review of Good Samaritan01-03; no imports or page changes.

entries.alt: A wounded barefoot traveler lies beside rocks on a dry road, wearing a torn light tunic with bruises and abrasions visible on his face and arm.
entries.caption: The wounded traveler lies alone beside the road after the attack in Jesus' parable. This imagined setting makes his need visible without adding a name or biography to the man Luke describes.
findings: Original-resolution image inspected. Curly dark hair, short beard, torn light tunic, forehead injury and abraded upper arm establish traveler continuity for02/03.
Non-graphic bruises/abrasions convey injury without exposed tissue or fresh gore. Torn garment retains modest coverage; no invented visible attack or assailants.
Side-lying body, resting hand, bent legs and overlapping bare feet plausible. Face appears pained and weak, not cheerful or posing; photorealistic skin, cloth, stones and daylight.

Luke10:30 describes stripping, wounding and abandonment half dead; modest garment is an artistic presentation choice. Caption does not convert appearance into medical diagnosis or exact historical portrait.
conditions: No invented private motives, historical portrait identity, diagnosis, recovery or exact geographical reconstruction claims.

entries.alt: The wounded traveler remains beside the rocks while an older gray-bearded man in light robes walks along the far side of the road.
entries.caption: The priest continues along the other side while the traveler remains on the ground. Jesus tells us that he saw the man and passed by, without explaining his private reasons.
findings: Traveler preserves01 facial/clothing/injury identity and prone position; dry rocky road continuity remains clear.
Older passerby has gray/white beard, light robe and brown mantle, distinct from younger Levite03. Feet and walking posture coherent; broad separation places him opposite traveler.
He is shown continuing away after seeing; this is not a claim his present gaze must remain fixed on the wounded man. No invented fear, ritual excuse, contempt or malice attributed.
Traveler visible hand/limbs remain coherent; injury restrained and non-graphic; daylight/materials photographic.
conditions: No invented private motives, historical portrait identity, diagnosis, recovery or exact geographical reconstruction claims.

entries.alt: A young clean-shaven passerby turns his head toward the wounded traveler while continuing along the opposite side of the road.
entries.caption: The Levite looks toward the injured traveler but continues past him. In Jesus' account, coming near and seeing the need do not yet become an act of care.
findings: Young Levite clean-shaven face and ochre clothing differ clearly from gray-bearded priest02. Head turns toward traveler while body/feet continue along opposite side; visual action fits seeing and passing.
Traveler retains dark curls, beard, torn sleeve and arm abrasion. Camera is now behind him; he partly props head/upper body to look toward passerby, remaining on the ground.

Raised head makes03 somewhat more alert than01/02, but does not show recovery, standing or capacity to resume travel. Half dead does not require continuous unconsciousness; no source contradiction sufficient to require revision. Keep later sequence consistent with severe need for assistance.
Supporting elbow/forearm and hand contact on ground plausible. Levite hands, sandals and legs coherent; no duplicated faces or limbs.
Luke10:32 records coming, looking and passing; exact pose and moment are artistic staging, and caption does not invent motive or relationship.
conditions: No invented private motives, historical portrait identity, diagnosis, recovery or exact geographical reconstruction claims.
